label: Autoland
description: TenHands' hadoku-task-automation pipeline. ONE board, one lane per repo. Spitball thoughts land untagged in the Inbox; the pipeline works out which repo they belong to and files them there. It then plans the work and writes the plan into notes, ending with `- [ ] Approve this plan`. Tick that box and the rest runs unattended: the change is implemented, gated, and arrives as a pull request. Pipeline state is the status chip on the card, not the lane — the lane only ever says which repo. You are asked for two things and no more: sign off the plan before the work, and merge the pull request after it.

statusKinds.means: The pipeline owns this right now.
Your move — a plan to sign off, or a pull request to merge.
Stuck in a way the pipeline cannot resolve. The reason is in notes.
Merged. The task is archived and leaves the board.

lanes.label: TenHands
lanes.description: Work targeting this repo. Drag a card here to re-file it.

_lanes: The lane set above is an EXAMPLE OF THE SHAPE, not a vocabulary to activate verbatim — `laneKind: "repo"` means the real lanes are the operator's repo list, built at activation time. One lane per repo, `editableBy: user` (a human must be able to re-file a card), and `repo` as `owner/name`. hadoku-task preserves unknown lane keys verbatim, so `repo` round-trips without their validator knowing it exists. A single lane is carried because `validateLaneSet` requires a non-empty array on BOTH sides and a preset that fails its own validator would be dropped from the picker; see autoland-v3.md §10 for the `lanes`-optional-on-a-preset resolution that removes this.
